title:
Spot the risk.
Prepare the response.
narration: When a river starts rising, the challenge is not just understanding the weather. It is getting the right people and equipment ready. This is Rescue Ops.

title: One workspace. One coordinated response.
narration: We are following a seeded flood preparedness exercise in Kenya's Tana River region. The coordinator starts with one operational picture: active missions, available resources, field reports and the people behind the response. These are demonstration records, not an active emergency. Every decision stays connected to its region and workspace.

title: A reason to look closer.
narration: Sentinel brings the evidence onto Disaster Radar before the coordinator asks a question. In this scenario, forecast rainfall and a rising gauge identify a place that deserves attention. Selecting a pin reveals its source, time and status. A forecast, a field observation and an official warning mean different things. A watch level is a reason to investigate, not a prediction of which streets will flood.

title: From evidence to a useful next step.
narration: Ask Sentinel turns that evidence into a practical conversation. Muse Wonder works through controlled backend tools. Numerical services calculate rainfall and threshold crossings; the model explains what changed, what is missing and what to check next. Here, the useful next step is to confirm the river level and prepare transport. The coordinator can inspect the evidence and the recorded tool steps behind the answer.

title: Make a mission the team can staff.
narration: Next, the coordinator turns that finding into a mission. Muse Spark helps collect the purpose, time, meeting point and required skills in ordinary language. Corrections stay in the draft, and missing details are brought back for review. The result is a mission that can be staged and staffed, with a clear brief and a confirmed assembly point.

title: The shortage is part of the answer.
narration: Spark then checks the mission against qualified applicants, equipment stock and existing commitments. In our exercise, one vehicle is already reserved. The proposal exposes the shortage instead of promising a vehicle that is not available. The coordinator reviews who is eligible, what can be allocated and what still needs arranging. The model recommends; it does not reserve equipment or dispatch a volunteer.

title: The coordinator decides.
narration: Before approval, the coordinator reviews the plan and confirms local conditions and access. The backend rechecks the mission, people, stock and linked weather evidence. Approved assignments and reservations are recorded together. The same evidence that raised the concern remains attached to the planning decision, while drafts and run history make the reasoning inspectable.

title: Investigate. Explain. Prepare.
narration: Wonder investigates. Spark helps prepare the team. The coordinator decides what happens in the field. Rescue Ops connects disaster intelligence to a response people can actually organise.
